# Halatto

> Vintage camera filter for iPhone: make photos you already took look shot on film, a disposable, instant, 90s or digital camera, with grain and a date stamp.

Halatto (App Store name "Vintage Photo Filter – Halatto") is an iPhone photo editor for photos already in the library. Each of its 14 looks simulates a whole old camera: film or sensor color, grain or noise, lens softness, vignette, flare and light leaks. Aging, flash, a frame and an orange date stamp go on top. Photos are edited on the iPhone, with no account and nothing uploaded. Free to try with a daily limit; iPhone only, iOS 18.6 or later.

## Frequently asked questions

- [How do I make my iPhone photos look like film?](https://halatto.app/guides/make-photos-look-like-film-on-iphone/): Open the photo in Halatto, pick a film look such as Titan 38 or Tungsten 800, and raise grain and film age a little. Film color, grain and the softness of an old lens are what make a photo read as film; a color filter alone does not.
- [Is there a disposable camera filter for photos I already took?](https://halatto.app/guides/disposable-camera-filter-on-iphone/): Yes. Many disposable camera apps only work when you shoot in them. In Halatto you open any photo from your library and choose Snap 400 or Snap Gold, then add the flash and the orange date stamp.
- [How do I get the Y2K digicam look on iPhone?](https://halatto.app/guides/digicam-filter-y2k-photos-on-iphone/): Pick one of the three digicam looks (Silver IX, Cyber Blue or Digi 2MP) and add the Digital flash. They add CCD color, sensor noise, cool whites and the hard flash of a 2000s compact camera.
- [How do I add a date stamp to a photo on iPhone?](https://halatto.app/guides/add-date-stamp-to-photo-on-iphone/): The Photos app cannot print a date on a picture. In Halatto open the photo, tap Date stamp and choose a corner: the orange date is taken from the day the photo was shot, and you can change its color, size and direction.
- [How can I make a photo look old?](https://halatto.app/guides/make-a-photo-look-old-on-iphone/): Use Aging: start with the Shoebox or Faded print preset, then raise Fade and Yellowing and add dust, stains or creases. A warm film look and a light leak finish the effect.
- [Can I get a Polaroid-style instant photo look?](https://halatto.app/guides/instant-photo-effect-on-iphone/): Yes. Halatto has three instant looks: SX Fold for the classic folding-camera color, Square 600 for the boxy instant look and Mini Instant for credit-card prints. Halatto is not affiliated with Polaroid or Fujifilm.
- [How do I add film grain to a photo on iPhone?](https://halatto.app/guides/add-film-grain-to-a-photo-on-iphone/): Every Halatto look has its own grain, and you can set the amount after you pick it. Grain looks most natural with a little fade and a softer lens, which the film looks add for you.
- [How do I put the same filter on many photos at once?](https://halatto.app/guides/apply-the-same-filter-to-multiple-photos-on-iphone/): Save your edit as a recipe, then use Develop the Roll: select the photos and tap Develop all to put the same camera on every one, so a trip looks like one roll of film.
- [Does Halatto upload my photos?](https://halatto.app/guides/best-vintage-camera-apps-for-iphone/#privacy): No. Photos are edited on your iPhone, there is no account, and nothing is uploaded to a server.
- [Is Halatto free, and which devices does it run on?](https://halatto.app/#faq): It is free to download, and every look and effect works up to a daily limit. A subscription or a lifetime purchase removes the limit. It requires iOS 18.6 or later on iPhone; there is no Android version.
- [Is there an Android version?](https://halatto.app/#faq): No. Halatto is published for iPhone on the Apple App Store only.
